correctness.rationale: For every \(0<r<1\), \(0\le T\le1\) and \(q>0\), the rank-one inverse preconditioner F_q is SPD with \(\det(F_q)=q\). The symmetric split operator has trace \(q+r+(1-q)(1-r)t\) and determinant \(rq\). Two-point Kantorovich sharpness converts this to the exact supremum over all nonzero initial errors. Optimizing \(q/(a q+b)^2\) on \(q\le1\), and \(q/(q+r)^2\) on \(q\ge1\), yields the unique global minimizer; direct algebra establishes the loss, nominal bound, and \(r\)-to-zero limit. Actual embedded verify.py run achieved 15444 exact identities, 2400 independently reconstructed first PCG worst-error steps, 850 randomized minimax samples and analytic frontier checks. The finite checks corroborate, not prove, the universal formula. Degenerate boundaries T=0 and T=1/2 are included. No assumptions on unknown direction distributions are smuggled into the quantifiers.

value.rationale: The uncertainty cap is motivated by how approximate extreme-eigenvector directions are estimated for low-rank spectral inverse preconditioners. This complete natural two-mode minimax shows exactly when any positive rank-one correction improves worst one-step PCG energy loss and when it must be switched off, with a surprisingly condition-number-independent \(45^\circ\) availability boundary. A distinct condition-number-sensitive threshold exposes when the common nominal exact-eigenvector coefficient is worse than no correction; a sharp small-curvature law quantifies the angular accuracy needed to retain fixed contraction. These are decision-relevant structural boundaries, not mere substitution or reported numerics. Scope restricted to one exact step in dimension two.
